name: Trinity
summary: A staged imaging-Cherenkov programme targets Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. A demonstrator telescope at Frisco Peak tests the technology before a proposed eighteen-telescope observatory.
physics_targets: Astrophysical neutrinos from approximately 1 PeV to 1 EeV
detection_principle: A tau emerging from the Earth can decay into an upward-going air shower. Telescopes pointed near the horizon would image the brief atmospheric Cherenkov flash with silicon-photomultiplier cameras.

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: The project states the demonstrator has taken data since October 2023 and describes the programme as the first of three development phases.

timeline.event: Demonstrator began taking data at Frisco Peak, Utah.

collaboration.name: Trinity Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

results.summary: Demonstrated camera, optics and remote-operation performance. The full observatory’s quoted neutrino sensitivity remains prospective.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
